claim: CasExpress is a system designed to drive fluorescent protein expression in cells that survive caspase-3 activation in Drosophila.
source: To document systematically where and when cells survive caspase-3 activation in vivo, we designed a system, CasExpress, which drives fluorescent protein expression, transiently or permanently, in cells that survive caspase-3 activation in Drosophila.
evidence: The abstract directly states the design and purpose of the CasExpress system.

claim: Widespread survival of caspase-3 activity was discovered using CasExpress.
source: We discovered widespread survival of caspase-3 activity.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a finding from the study.

claim: Some cells activated caspase-3 during their normal development in every cell and in every animal without evidence of apoptosis.
source: Some cells activated caspase-3 during their normal development in every cell and in every animal without evidence of apoptosis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes this pattern of caspase-3 activation.

claim: In the brain, CasExpress expression was sporadic both temporally and spatially and overlapped with periods of apoptosis.
source: In other tissues, such as the brain, expression was sporadic both temporally and spatially and overlapped with periods of apoptosis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the pattern observed in the brain.

claim: In adults, reporter expression was evident in a large fraction of cells in most tissues of every animal.
source: In adults, reporter expression was evident in a large fraction of cells in most tissues of every animal; however the precise patterns varied.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this observation about adult tissues.

claim: Inhibition of caspase activity in wing discs reduced wing size.
source: Inhibition of caspase activity in wing discs reduced wing size demonstrating functional significance.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this experimental result.

claim: Caspase-3 carries out the executioner phase of apoptosis.
source: Caspase-3 carries out the executioner phase of apoptosis, however under special circumstances, cells can survive its activity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Under special circumstances, cells can survive caspase-3 activity.
source: Caspase-3 carries out the executioner phase of apoptosis, however under special circumstances, cells can survive its activity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Apoptosis was originally described as a series of morphological changes that cells undergo as they die.
source: The cell death program known as apoptosis was originally described as a series of morphological changes that cells undergo as they die (Tenev et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as historical background with a citation.

claim: Caspases emerged as key regulators and executioners of apoptosis.
source: The reproducibility of the sequence suggested an underlying molecular program, and a conserved set of enzymes, the caspases, emerged as key regulators and executioners of apoptosis (Martin and Green, 1995; Jacobson and Evan, 1994; Thornberry, 1998).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Caspase activation is frequently a terminal event resulting in swift cellular demise.
source: While caspase activation is frequently a terminal event resulting in swift cellular demise (Chang et al., 2002), cell survival following caspase activation has been described (e.g., [Florentin and Arama, 2012; Kuranaga and Miura, 2007; Kumar, 2004; Meinander et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Cell survival following caspase activation has been described.
source: While caspase activation is frequently a terminal event resulting in swift cellular demise (Chang et al., 2002), cell survival following caspase activation has been described (e.g., [Florentin and Arama, 2012; Kuranaga and Miura, 2007; Kumar, 2004; Meinander et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: In some cells and tissues, caspases promote localized or partial destruction of the cell without actually killing it.
source: In some cells and tissues, caspases promote localized or partial destruction of the cell without actually killing it (Arama et al., 2003; Huh et al., 2004; Connolly et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: A variety of primary cells and cell lines can survive caspase activation following a lethal dose of an apoptotic stimulus, as long as it is transient and thus sublethal in time.
source: A variety of primary cells and cell lines can survive caspase activation following a lethal dose of an apoptotic stimulus, as long as it is transient and thus sublethal in time (Tang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The reversal of late stage apoptosis has been named anastasis.
source: This reversal of late stage apoptosis has been named anastasis (Greek for 'rising to life').
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the introduction.

claim: Cell survival following caspase activation in response to a sublethal dose of irradiation has been reported.
source: Cell survival following caspase activation in response to a sublethal dose of irradiation has also been reported (Florentin and Arama, 2012; Liu et al., 2015; Ichim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Cell survival following caspase activation may limit permanent damage to the heart following transient ischemia.
source: It may limit permanent damage to the heart following transient ischemia (Kenis et al., 2010); however it can also be oncogenic (Tang et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2015; Ichim et al., 2015), and could in principle allow tumor cells to escape chemotherapy.
evidence: This is stated as a potential beneficial effect with a citation.

claim: Cell survival following caspase activation can be oncogenic.
source: It may limit permanent damage to the heart following transient ischemia (Kenis et al., 2010); however it can also be oncogenic (Tang et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2015; Ichim et al., 2015), and could in principle allow tumor cells to escape chemotherapy.
evidence: This is stated as a potential harmful effect with citations.

claim: Cell survival following caspase activation could allow tumor cells to escape chemotherapy.
source: It may limit permanent damage to the heart following transient ischemia (Kenis et al., 2010); however it can also be oncogenic (Tang et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2015; Ichim et al., 2015), and could in principle allow tumor cells to escape chemotherapy.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative possibility.

claim: Apoptosis is a critical feature of normal development in multicellular organisms.
source: Apoptosis is a critical feature of normal development in multicellular organisms (Miura, 2012; Denton and Kumar, 2015; Vaux and Korsmeyer, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Studies in model organisms such as worms and flies have made important contributions to unraveling the mechanisms of apoptosis.
source: Studies in model organisms such as worms and flies have made important contributions to unraveling the underlying mechanisms (Connolly et al., 2014; Denton and Kumar, 2015; Orme and Meier, 2009; Steller, 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: It is unknown whether cells ever recover from the brink of apoptotic cell death during development.
source: It is unknown whether cells ever recover from the brink of apoptotic cell death during development.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: CasExpress is a genetic system to mark and manipulate cells that survive caspase activation in Drosophila.
source: Therefore we developed a genetic system to mark and manipulate cells that survive caspase activation in Drosophila (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a method developed in the study, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: The majority of cells in the adult derive from cells that survive caspase activation during normal development.
source: Using these CasExpress transgenic flies, we discovered that the majority of cells in the adult derive from cells that survive caspase activation during normal development.
evidence: This is stated as a major finding from the study.

claim: In some organs, every cell activated the sensor over an extended period of development without evidence of apoptosis or morphological remodeling.
source: For example, in some organs, every cell activated the sensor over an extended period of development without evidence of apoptosis or morphological remodeling, suggesting a function for caspase-3 unrelated to cellular destruction.
evidence: This is stated as an observed pattern in the introduction.

claim: In some tissues, caspase-3 has a function unrelated to cellular destruction.
source: For example, in some organs, every cell activated the sensor over an extended period of development without evidence of apoptosis or morphological remodeling, suggesting a function for caspase-3 unrelated to cellular destruction.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observed pattern.

claim: In some tissues, CasExpress activation was sporadic in temporal and spatial pattern.
source: In other tissues, activation was sporadic in temporal and spatial pattern, suggesting a stochastic process.
evidence: This is stated as an observed pattern in the introduction.

claim: Sporadic CasExpress activation suggests a stochastic process.
source: In other tissues, activation was sporadic in temporal and spatial pattern, suggesting a stochastic process.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observed pattern.

claim: In tissues with sporadic activation, the precise patterns differed from animal to animal.
source: In these tissues, the precise patterns differed from animal to animal, and occurred in regions that normally exhibit apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the introduction.

claim: Sporadic CasExpress activation occurred in regions that normally exhibit apoptosis.
source: In these tissues, the precise patterns differed from animal to animal, and occurred in regions that normally exhibit apoptosis.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the introduction.

claim: Some cells recover from the brink of apoptotic cell death and undergo developmental anastasis.
source: These observations suggest that some cells recover from the brink of apoptotic cell death and undergo developmental anastasis.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observations.

claim: Different patterns of CasExpress activation represent distinct functions of executioner caspases during normal development.
source: We propose that these different patterns represent distinct functions of executioner caspases during normal development.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on the observations.

claim: CasExpress is a caspase-inducible Gal4 transcription factor.
source: In order to detect and follow the fates of cells that survive caspase activation, we designed a caspase-inducible Gal4 transcription factor (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the design with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Gal4 is tethered to the plasma membrane by fusion to mCD8 to keep it inactive in the absence of caspase activity.
source: To keep Gal4 inactive in the absence of caspase activity, we tethered it to the plasma membrane by fusing it to mCD8 (mouse cluster of differentiation 8).
evidence: This is stated as a design feature of the system.

claim: The caspase-3-binding and cleavage domain from DIAP1 was inserted between CD8 and Gal4 to render the protein caspase-inducible.
source: To render the protein caspase-inducible, we inserted the caspase-3-binding and cleavage domain from the Drosophila Inhibitor of Apoptosis Protein 1 (DIAP1) (Ditzel et al., 2003) in between CD8 and Gal4.
evidence: This is stated as a design feature of the system with a citation.

claim: A DQVA control transgene was created with a DQVD to DQVA amino acid substitution to render it caspase insensitive.
source: As a negative control we created a second transgene with a DQVD to DQVA amino acid substitution in the caspase cleavage site (Figure 1B) in order to render it caspase insensitive, hereafter the 'DQVA control.'
evidence: This is stated as a description of the control with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The fusion protein was expressed under the control of the ubiquitin enhancer/promoter.
source: To allow for detection of caspase activation in as many cell types as possible, the fusion protein was expressed under the control of the ubiquitin (ubi) enhancer/promoter.
evidence: This is stated as a design feature of the system.

claim: The attP40 landing site allows relatively uniform, moderate levels of expression in a variety of tissues.
source: We characterized the expression and activity of transgenic flies bearing a site-directed insertion into the attP40 landing site, selected for its ability to allow relatively uniform, moderate levels of expression in a variety of tissues (Markstein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for site selection with a citation.

claim: G-Trace expresses two fluorescent protein targets under the control of Gal4-responsive UAS.
source: To detect caspase activity, we crossed the sensor and control to G-Trace (Evans et al., 2009) a fly line that expresses two fluorescent protein targets, under the control of Gal4-responsive UAS (upstream activating sequences).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the G-Trace system with a citation.

claim: G-Trace contains three transgenes: UAS-RFP, UAS-FLP, and ubi-FRT-STOP-FRT-GFP.
source: G-Trace flies contain three transgenes, all on the second chromosome: UAS-RFP, UAS-FLP, which encodes a yeast recombinase enzyme, and a ubi-FRT-STOP-FRT-GFP cassette where FRT stands for FLP Recombination Target sequence.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the G-Trace components.

claim: Crossing the mCD8-DQVD-Gal4 sensor to G-Trace leads to permanent GFP expression in any cell that survives transient caspase activation and in all of its progeny.
source: Crossing the mCD8-DQVD-Gal4 sensor to G-Trace should lead to permanent GFP expression in any cell that survives transient caspase activation and in all of its progeny, in contrast to other caspase activity reporters (Bardet et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as an expected outcome with a citation.

claim: RFP expression is transient and limited to the cells that activated caspase-3 but not their progeny.
source: We expected the caspase-activated Gal4 protein to be short-lived because we had observed rapid degradation of other caspase reporters (Tang et al., 2012), so we anticipated RFP would be transient and limited to the cells that activated caspase-3 but not their progeny.
evidence: This is stated as an expectation based on prior observations with a citation.

claim: Widespread GFP expression was found in adult tissues.
source: We first examined adult tissues where, to our surprise, we found widespread GFP expression (Figure 1C–L).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1C-L.

claim: In the proventriculus, GFP was evident but little RFP was evident, suggesting that caspase had been active earlier during development.
source: In the intestine for example, GFP was evident in the most anterior structure, the proventriculus (Figure 1C), although little RFP was evident there, suggesting that caspase had been active earlier during development.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: In the midgut, both RFP and GFP appeared in a partially overlapping pattern.
source: In the midgut both RFP and GFP appeared in a partially overlapping pattern (Figure 1C,D–D").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1C, D-D".

claim: Large nuclei corresponding to differentiated epithelial cells in the midgut expressed both RFP and GFP suggesting ongoing caspase activation.
source: Large nuclei corresponding to differentiated epithelial cells expressed both RFP and GFP suggesting ongoing caspase activation, whereas a subset of small progenitor cells expressed GFP but not RFP (Figure 1D–D" arrows).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation with reference to Figure 1D-D".

claim: A subset of small progenitor cells in the midgut expressed GFP but not RFP.
source: Large nuclei corresponding to differentiated epithelial cells expressed both RFP and GFP suggesting ongoing caspase activation, whereas a subset of small progenitor cells expressed GFP but not RFP (Figure 1D–D" arrows).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1D-D".

claim: Visceral muscle and hindgut showed a mixture of GFP+/RFP- cells as well as some GFP+/RFP+ cells.
source: Visceral muscle and hindgut showed a mixture of GFP+/RFP- cells as well as some GFP+/RFP+ cells (Figure 1E–F").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1E-F".

claim: The adult eye and antenna exhibited widespread nuclear GFP but only infrequent RFP.
source: The adult eye and antenna exhibited widespread nuclear GFP but only infrequent RFP (Figure 1G–H"), suggesting that caspase had been activated earlier in development either in a large fraction of cells, or in precursors that gave rise to a large fraction of adult cells; however little activation of caspase appeared to be ongoing in the adult.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1G-H".

claim: In the adult eye and antenna, caspase had been activated earlier in development either in a large fraction of cells, or in precursors that gave rise to a large fraction of adult cells.
source: The adult eye and antenna exhibited widespread nuclear GFP but only infrequent RFP (Figure 1G–H"), suggesting that caspase had been activated earlier in development either in a large fraction of cells, or in precursors that gave rise to a large fraction of adult cells; however little activation of caspase appeared to be ongoing in the adult.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: Little activation of caspase appeared to be ongoing in the adult eye and antenna.
source: The adult eye and antenna exhibited widespread nuclear GFP but only infrequent RFP (Figure 1G–H"), suggesting that caspase had been activated earlier in development either in a large fraction of cells, or in precursors that gave rise to a large fraction of adult cells; however little activation of caspase appeared to be ongoing in the adult.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: In the adult central brain and nerve cord, a minority of cells expressed GFP and/or RFP.
source: In the adult central brain and nerve cord, a minority of cells expressed GFP and/or RFP (Figure 1I–J").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1I-J".

claim: In the optic lobe, many but not all cells expressed GFP and/or RFP.
source: In the optic lobe, many but not all cells expressed GFP and/or RFP (Figure 1I–I"), whereas in body wall muscle, nearly every cell expressed GFP (Figure 1K–K").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1I-I".

claim: In body wall muscle, nearly every cell expressed GFP.
source: In the optic lobe, many but not all cells expressed GFP and/or RFP (Figure 1I–I"), whereas in body wall muscle, nearly every cell expressed GFP (Figure 1K–K").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1K-K".

claim: In the female reproductive system, every cell of the oviduct was GFP+/RFP- in every animal.
source: In the female reproductive system, every cell of the oviduct was GFP+/RFP- in every animal, whereas the majority of germline and somatic cells in egg chambers lacked FP expression (Figure 1L).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1L.

claim: The majority of germline and somatic cells in egg chambers lacked FP expression.
source: In the female reproductive system, every cell of the oviduct was GFP+/RFP- in every animal, whereas the majority of germline and somatic cells in egg chambers lacked FP expression (Figure 1L).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1L.

claim: In Drosophila embryos, the only tissue that activated CasExpress robustly was the salivary gland beginning at stage 12.
source: In Drosophila embryos, the only tissue that activated CasExpress robustly was the salivary gland beginning at stage 12 (Figure 2A–A").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2A-A".

claim: Salivary gland expression was not detected in the DQVA control.
source: Salivary gland expression was not detected in the DQVA control, demonstrating that this was not due to leaky or background expression from the G-Trace transgenes or random breakdown of the fusion protein that might separate Gal4 from the transmembrane domain.
evidence: This is stated as an observation that validates the specificity of the sensor.

claim: The DQVD sensor and DQVA control showed similar patterns and levels of fusion protein expression at the cell surface throughout the embryo and in most tissues and stages of development.
source: We also confirmed that the DQVD sensor and DQVA control showed similar patterns and levels of fusion protein expression at the cell surface detected with anti-mCD8 antibody staining throughout the embryo and in most tissues and stages of development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: RFP was detected in some randomly distributed cells in the embryo, likely corresponding to a subset of cells that normally undergo apoptosis.
source: In the embryo RFP was also detected in some randomly distributed cells, likely corresponding to a subset of cells that normally undergo apoptosis (Figure 2A and A"); little if any GFP was detected in those cells, presumably because dying cells were not active enough to transcribe and translate FLP, undergo DNA recombination, and then transcribe and translate GFP to detectable levels.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation with reference to Figure 2A and A".

claim: Little if any GFP was detected in randomly distributed RFP+ cells in the embryo, presumably because dying cells were not active enough to transcribe and translate FLP, undergo DNA recombination, and then transcribe and translate GFP to detectable levels.
source: In the embryo RFP was also detected in some randomly distributed cells, likely corresponding to a subset of cells that normally undergo apoptosis (Figure 2A and A"); little if any GFP was detected in those cells, presumably because dying cells were not active enough to transcribe and translate FLP, undergo DNA recombination, and then transcribe and translate GFP to detectable levels.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: RFP was detected in the salivary gland beginning in stage 12, and GFP expression became evident later.
source: While RFP was detected in the salivary gland beginning in stage 12, GFP expression became evident later (Figure 2B–B"), confirming that these FPs exhibit different timing of activation.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2B-B".

claim: RFP and GFP exhibit different timing of activation.
source: While RFP was detected in the salivary gland beginning in stage 12, GFP expression became evident later (Figure 2B–B"), confirming that these FPs exhibit different timing of activation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observation.

claim: Flies expressing the DQVD sensor were viable and fertile and showed no discernible morphological defects.
source: Although the DQVD and DQVA proteins contained the caspase binding sequence from DIAP1 (Tenev et al., 2005), which in principle could function as a dominant-negative inhibitor of caspase activity if expressed at high enough levels, the flies expressing the sensor were viable and fertile and showed no discernible morphological defects.
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: There was no decrease in the number, or change in distribution, of apoptotic cells in DQVD and DQVA embryos compared to w1118 embryos.
source: Moreover, there was no decrease in the number, or change in distribution, of apoptotic cells in DQVD and DQVA embryos compared to w1118 embryos (Figure 2C–C").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2C-C".

claim: Both RFP and GFP continued to be expressed throughout embryonic and larval development.
source: Both RFP and GFP continued to be expressed throughout embryonic and larval development (Figure 2D–F").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2D-F".

claim: During larval development CasExpress activation appeared over time in many cell types and tissues including all imaginal discs, oenocytes, and in subsets of neurons.
source: During larval development CasExpress activation appeared over time in many cell types and tissues including all imaginal discs, oenocytes, and in subsets of neurons (Figure 2E and Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figures 2E and 3.

claim: Tissues from flies carrying G-Trace in the absence of the caspase sensor or in combination with the DQVA caspase-insensitive control exhibited infrequent FP expression in small clones in a minority of animals.
source: Tissues from flies carrying G-Trace in the absence of the caspase sensor or in combination with the DQVA caspase-insensitive control exhibited infrequent FP expression in small clones in a minority of animals (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The frequency and patterns of background FP expression were very similar regardless of the presence or absence of the DQVA control transgene.
source: The frequency and patterns were very similar regardless of the presence or absence of the DQVA control transgene (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), suggesting that this minor background was due to leaky, Gal-4-independent FLP expression from the UAS-FLP transgene.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Minor background FP expression was due to leaky, Gal-4-independent FLP expression from the UAS-FLP transgene.
source: The frequency and patterns were very similar regardless of the presence or absence of the DQVA control transgene (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), suggesting that this minor background was due to leaky, Gal-4-independent FLP expression from the UAS-FLP transgene.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: Expression in the presence of the DQVD caspase-sensitive construct was present in every animal.
source: In contrast, expression in the presence of the DQVD caspase-sensitive construct was present in every animal (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and in large fractions of cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3.

claim: Oenocytes exhibited RFP and GFP expression in virtually every cell and in every animal.
source: For example oenocytes exhibited RFP and GFP expression in virtually every cell and in every animal (Figure 3A–A").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3A-A".

claim: In imaginal discs fewer cells expressed RFP as compared to GFP.
source: In contrast, in imaginal discs fewer cells expressed RFP as compared to GFP (Figure 3B–D").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3B-D".

claim: Every imaginal disc from every animal exhibited CasExpress expression, but the precise patterns varied.
source: Although every disc from every animal exhibited expression, the precise patterns varied (Figure 3—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplements 2–4.

claim: In the developing CNS the patterns of CasExpress expression were not bilaterally symmetric.
source: In the developing central nervous system (CNS) the patterns were not bilaterally symmetric (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In imaginal discs the patterns of CasExpress expression, particularly of RFP, varied from animal to animal and did not appear to correspond to known developmental patterns of known signaling pathways or cell types.
source: In the imaginal discs the patterns, particularly of RFP, varied from animal to animal and did not appear to correspond to known developmental patterns of known signaling pathways or cell types (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Tissues that showed little or no activation of the sensor during normal development up through the third instar included somatic muscles, trachea, and the ventral nerve cord.
source: Tissues that showed little or no activation of the sensor during normal development up through the third instar included somatic muscles, trachea, and the ventral nerve cord (Figure 3E–E").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3E-E".

claim: A consistently large fraction (50–80%) of cells in the developing optic lobes were GFP-positive.
source: Although most of the nervous system showed little sensor activation, a consistently large fraction (50–80%) of cells in the developing optic lobes were GFP-positive (Figure 3E–E").
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3E-E".

claim: In the larval intestine, partially overlapping GFP and RFP expression patterns were observed.
source: In the larval intestine, partially overlapping GFP and RFP expression patterns were observed (Figure 3F), and while the overall regional patterns were conserved from one animal to the other, the details varied (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: In the larval intestine, while the overall regional patterns of CasExpress expression were conserved from one animal to the other, the details varied.
source: In the larval intestine, partially overlapping GFP and RFP expression patterns were observed (Figure 3F), and while the overall regional patterns were conserved from one animal to the other, the details varied (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The dronc mutant background eliminated caspase activity detected with an antibody against cleaved and activated Dcp-1.
source: As expected, the homozygous dronc mutant background eliminated caspase activity detected with an antibody against cleaved and activated Dcp-1 (c-Dcp-1) (Figure 4A–F').
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4A-F'.

claim: The dronc mutant eliminated virtually all RFP and GFP expression in imaginal discs from CasExpress.
source: The dronc mutant also eliminated virtually all RFP and GFP expression in imaginal discs from CasExpress (Figure 4A–F).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4A-F.

claim: Homozygous dronc mutant embryos retained RFP and GFP expression in the salivary gland, possibly due to the perdurance of maternal caspase expression.
source: Homozygous dronc mutant embryos retained RFP and GFP expression in the salivary gland, possibly due to the perdurance of maternal caspase expression.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation.

claim: Embryonic salivary glands label with an antibody against cleaved caspase-3.
source: To confirm the presence of cleaved caspase in embryonic salivary gland cells, which has not been previously reported, we stained CasExpress embryos with an antibody against cleaved caspase-3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). Despite the absence of other apoptotic markers in these cells, salivary glands did label with this antibody, suggesting a non-apoptotic function for caspase in this tissue.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of cleaved caspase-3 in embryonic salivary glands suggests a non-apoptotic function for caspase in this tissue.
source: To confirm the presence of cleaved caspase in embryonic salivary gland cells, which has not been previously reported, we stained CasExpress embryos with an antibody against cleaved caspase-3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). Despite the absence of other apoptotic markers in these cells, salivary glands did label with this antibody, suggesting a non-apoptotic function for caspase in this tissue.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: The Baculovirus p35 protein inhibits both executioner caspases DrIce and Dcp-1, but not Dronc.
source: The Baculovirus p35 protein inhibits both executioner caspases DrIce and Dcp-1, but not Dronc (Meier et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: GMR-p35 significantly reduced the number of RFP+ cells in the posterior eye disc compared to the control.
source: GMR-p35 significantly reduced the number of RFP+ cells in the posterior eye disc compared to the control (Figure 4 G-I), whereas no change in RFP was observed in the antennal disc, which served as an additional internal control.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4 G-I.

claim: No change in RFP was observed in the antennal disc when GMR-p35 was expressed, which served as an additional internal control.
source: GMR-p35 significantly reduced the number of RFP+ cells in the posterior eye disc compared to the control (Figure 4 G-I), whereas no change in RFP was observed in the antennal disc, which served as an additional internal control.
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: The few remaining RFP+ cells in the posterior eye disc with GMR-p35 likely were cells that had activated Gal4 prior to the onset of expression of the GMR promoter.
source: The few remaining RFP+ cells in the posterior eye disc likely were cells that had activated Gal4 prior to the onset of expression of the GMR promoter.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: GFP expression was still evident in the posterior eye disc with GMR-p35, indicating that caspase activation preceded expression of p35 from the GMR enhancer/promoter in those cells.
source: GFP expression was still evident, indicating that caspase activation preceded expression of p35 from the GMR enhancer/promoter in those cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The upstream caspase Dredd activates NFkB signaling and expression of anti-microbial peptides.
source: One known non-apoptotic role for caspase activity is in the innate immune response. Specifically the upstream caspase Dredd activates NFkB signaling and expression of anti-microbial peptides (Meinander et al., 2012; Leulier et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: No difference in GFP or RFP expression level or pattern was detected between dredd mutants and heterozygous wild type siblings in any tissue examined.
source: Therefore to determine whether the CasExpress activity we detected in the gut was due to the immune response, we crossed CasExpress into dredd mutant animals. However we detected no difference in the GFP or RFP expression level or pattern between dredd mutants and heterozygous wild type siblings, in any tissue examined (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: When flies carrying CasExpress, Gal80ts, and G-TRACE were grown at 18°C, GFP was completely repressed.
source: When flies carrying CasExpress, Gal80ts, and G-TRACE were grown at 18°C, GFP was completely repressed, and even the infrequent, random clones due to leaky expression of UAS-FLP was suppressed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Caspase was activated sporadically in time in imaginal discs.
source: Rather than all the GFP+ cells arising at one particular stage, sporadic expression was observed regardless of when the temperature shift occurred. This was true in wing (Figure 5A–C), leg (Figure 5D–F) and eye-antennal discs (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 5A-I.
